dismissed_hits.reason: Its continuous-time irrational-orbit alignment counterexample is unrelated to the finite Klein-group action on grid positions.
Its failed tournament induction under vertex re-addition has no analogue in this non-inductive finite enumeration.
Its omitted-correlation hypothesis concerns probabilistic family mixtures; the present counts are deterministic, and the once-or-twice multiplicity hypothesis is explicit.
Its spanning-tree cut-crossing error concerns edge connectivity and tree deletion; this proof uses neither cuts nor spanning trees.
Its counterexample concerns overlapping consecutive windows in an ordered 52-card deck. No windows are counted here, and physical-card multiplicities are handled explicitly.
Its noncommutative set-factorization reversal is unrelated: reverse transformation types here are constructed explicitly from reversed ordered pairs, not inferred by swapping factors.
Its warning applies to conditionally convergent infinite series; every sum and reordering here is a finite integer count.
Its binomial-cancellation error is unrelated to the finite double count over 24 orbit orders, whose incidence values were checked term by term.

results.claim: Swish containment is exactly a multiplicity-respecting directed-cycle problem.
results.proof_sketch: For any candidate subcollection, fix one allowed transformation of each physical card and direct its arc from hoop to ball. In a Swish, every used position has indegree and outdegree exactly one, so each nonempty component is a directed simple cycle and the cards of any component are themselves a Swish. Conversely, distinct physical cards realizing a directed simple cycle put exactly one hoop and one ball at every cycle vertex. Thus a collection contains a Swish exactly when it can realize a directed simple cycle within its card-type multiplicities. Acting on the three applicable directed-graph hits, an exact regression check confirmed that p→q and q→p form a two-card Swish, either singleton does not, and adding an extra arc can make the whole selected set fail the Swish degree condition without destroying the contained two-card Swish. No transitive-closure or transitive-reduction inference is used.

results.claim: A no-swish collection contains at most 20 distinct transformation types, and this is sharp.
results.proof_sketch: The position orbits are A={(1,1),(1,3),(4,1),(4,3)}, B={(1,2),(4,2)}, C={(2,1),(2,3),(3,1),(3,3)}, and D={(2,2),(3,2)}. Exact enumeration gives 36 card types: eight internal types in classes of sizes 3,1,3,1 and 28 cross-orbit types in 14 reversal pairs. Both members of a reversal pair realize opposite arcs, hence a two-cycle. On either four-position orbit, the three internal types correspond to the three nonidentity elements of the Klein four group and together realize a directed triangle. Therefore an acyclic support has at most 14+2+1+2+1=20 types. Equality is attained by ordering A<B<C<D, taking all 14 cross types directed forward, and taking the six internal representatives (1,1)→(1,3), (1,1)→(4,1), (1,2)→(4,2), (2,1)→(2,3), (2,1)→(3,1), and (2,2)→(3,2), one card each. Cross arcs strictly advance the orbit order, while exact local cycle enumeration verifies that the six internal cards contain no cycle.

results.claim: Unless all eight internal types are duplicated, the usual once-or-twice interpretation of the 60-card deck already yields a 29-card no-swish subset.
results.proof_sketch: Assume explicitly that all 36 types occur with multiplicity one or two. Let M0 be the total multiplicity of the eight internal types. If at least one is not doubled, M0≤15, leaving at least 45 cross cards. For each of the 24 orders of A,B,C,D, select the six safe internal cards above and every physical cross card pointing forward. Each cross type is forward in exactly 12 orders, so the average selected cross-card count is (60−M0)/2≥45/2. Some integral count is therefore at least 23, giving at least 29 selected cards. A cycle cannot use a cross arc because orbit rank would strictly increase, and the internal selection is cycle-free. If the constructed set has more than 29 cards, discard arbitrary extras. This remains only a conditional theorem because the authorized input does not identify the actual deck's duplicated types.

results.claim: The authorized input omits information essential to deciding the exact commercial-deck target.
results.proof_sketch: The source supplies 60 cards and 36 types but not the duplicated-type identities. Under the once-or-twice convention, let Deck X double all eight internal types and both directions in eight reversal pairs. Any no-Swish subset uses at most 2,1,2,1 internal cards, at most two cards from each doubled pair, and at most one from each remaining pair, so it has at most 6+16+6=28 cards; a forward-order construction attains 28. Let Deck Y double nine forward cross types, all 14 reverse cross types, and one internal type. It has 60 cards, and two copies of the nine chosen forward types, one copy of each other forward type, and the six safe internal cards give an acyclic set of size 18+5+6=29. Both models have 36 present types, 24 duplicated types, 60 physical cards, and a 28-card no-Swish subset, yet their answers differ. Thus the authorized aggregates cannot decide the actual commercial deck.

final_writeup:
Transform each physical card and orient an arc from its hoop to its ball. A collection contains a Swish exactly when a directed simple cycle can be realized by distinct physical cards from it. Indeed, a Swish gives indegree and outdegree one at every used position and therefore decomposes into directed cycles; the cards of any one component are themselves a Swish. Conversely, any directed cycle supplies exactly one hoop and one ball at every cycle vertex. This characterization respects multiplicity because every occurrence of a cycle arc requires a distinct physical copy. In particular, opposite arcs form a valid two-card Swish. Extra selected cards may make the larger set fail the Swish degree condition, but they do not destroy containment because they can be discarded.

The twelve positions have four transformation orbits A,B,C,D of sizes 4,2,4,2. Exact enumeration gives 36 transformation types. Eight are internal to one position orbit, in classes of sizes 3,1,3,1; the other 28 form 14 cross-orbit reversal pairs. A no-Swish support contains at most one member of each reversal pair, since a pair makes a directed two-cycle, and at most two members of either internal triple, since a complete triple makes a directed triangle. Thus its support has at most

14+2+1+2+1=20

types. This is sharp: order A<B<C<D, choose all fourteen cross types pointing forward, and choose the six internal types represented by

(1,1)→(1,3), (1,1)→(4,1), (1,2)→(4,2),
(2,1)→(2,3), (2,1)→(3,1), (2,2)→(3,2).

Cross arcs cannot lie on a cycle because they strictly increase orbit rank, and exact local enumeration shows that the six internal cards contain no multiplicity-respecting cycle.

There is a useful conditional consequence. Suppose every type occurs once or twice. Since 60=36+24, exactly 24 types are doubled. If not all eight internal types are doubled, they account for at most 15 cards, leaving at least 45 cross cards. Average the forward cross-card count over all 24 orders of A,B,C,D. Every directed cross type is forward in exactly 12 orders, so some order selects at least ceil(45/2)=23 physical cross cards. Together with the six safe internal cards this gives at least 29 no-Swish cards; discard extras if necessary. Consequently, any once-or-twice commercial deck in which every 29 cards contain a Swish must duplicate all eight internal types.

This does not decide the requested commercial-deck question, because the authorized source does not say which types are duplicated. The omission is decisive. A compatible Deck X doubles all eight internal types and both directions in eight reversal pairs. Local two-cycle and triangle obstructions bound every no-Swish subset by 6+2·8+6=28, and a forward construction attains 28. A compatible Deck Y doubles nine forward cross types, all fourteen reverse types, and one internal type. Choosing both copies of those nine forward types, one copy of each other forward type, and the six safe internal cards gives 18+5+6=29 cycle-free cards. Both decks have 60 cards, contain all 36 types, use only multiplicities one and two, and contain a 28-card no-Swish subset, yet their answers differ.

Therefore the verified work is material but partial: it reduces the problem, proves the sharp 20-type support bound, isolates a broad conditional 29-card construction, and proves that the supplied aggregate deck description is insufficient. It neither certifies 28 for the actual commercial deck nor exhibits 29 actual commercial cards. The target remains unresolved until the commercial deck's 36-entry multiplicity vector is supplied.
